A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, and appendices A–K are readable and support reliable matching despite additions and renumbering.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendices J–K report original synthetic classification experiments, including margin and directional-convergence results in Figures 1–4.

after.justification: V2 retains the original synthetic experiments and adds MNIST experiments with a two-layer neural network in Section 5 and Appendix K.1.

M1.justification: The stochastic steepest-descent updates, momentum, SVRG-style estimator, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. The neural-network experiment applies existing optimizers; Appendix H.1 clarifies the canonical spectral direction already used rather than introducing a new update.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates synthetic Gaussian and orthogonal scale-skewed classification data. V2 retains these and adds MNIST digit classification, substantially extending coverage from constructed data to real images.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged. The added MNIST comparison uses existing Spectral-SGD/Muon and variance-reduced variants; Figure 5 explicitly defines SGDM as Spectral-SGD with momentum, not an additional baseline.

E3.justification: The new MNIST protocol uses 1,000 balanced samples, a width-100 two-layer sigmoid network, batch sizes {10, 100, 500, 1000}, and momentum {0, 0.5, 0.9}. It tracks a margin normalized by the maximum layer spectral norm, introducing a substantially different evaluation design. Existing synthetic protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 5 extends batch-size and momentum sensitivity analysis, with and without variance reduction, to nonlinear MNIST training. This adds evidence about stability outside the synthetic linear setting while retaining the existing sensitivity analyses and per-sample case study.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical tests. The added MNIST trajectories likewise have no reported uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Figure 5 adds the first real-data neural-network results: without momentum, batch size 10 retains a negative spectral margin while full-batch training reaches a positive margin; momentum and variance reduction mitigate this gap. These are substantial new results under new conditions. Figures 1–4 retain their plotted results.

T1.justification: V2 derives that Theorem 4.1's condition forces m = 1 because γ ≤ 2R, and adds Proposition 4.2 with its proof in Proposition D.6, establishing SignSGD failure on a separable two-sample dataset. Lemma H.1 also replaces equality of spectral and Frobenius argmax sets with a shared canonical direction. The momentum and variance-reduction bounds remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, first contribution, and conclusion replace the claimed large-mini-batch no-momentum guarantee with a full-batch-only guarantee and a failure counterexample at m = 2. This substantially narrows and redefines a central contribution; the other principal claims remain.

C2.justification: V1 describes the no-momentum batch condition as potentially conservative. V2 recognizes that it permits only full-batch training and explains that the counterexample does not characterize all stochastic dynamics. It also makes the batch–momentum trade-off more explicit and qualifies variance-reduction slowdown as a worst-case bound.

D1.justification: V2 documents the added MNIST experiment's class-balanced sampling, hidden width, sigmoid activation, cross-entropy loss, and parameter grids. These are localized reproducibility additions for a new experiment; the earlier algorithmic and experimental details are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds dedicated discussions of stochastic margin maximization and variance reduction, distinguishing the work from SGD, momentum SGD, and stochastic AdaGrad-Norm analyses and stating specific novelty claims. The no-momentum rate corollary is now explicitly attributed to Fan et al. (2025), materially revising its positioning.

P1.justification: V2 locally rewrites Section 4.1, expands related-work and experimental discussion, revises appendix headings and the contents listing, and corrects wording and cross-references. Most prose and the overall document organization remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds the six-panel Figure 5 and adjusts caption formatting and figure placement. Figures 3 and 4 correct their stated geometries from ℓ2 to ℓ∞ and spectral, respectively. Figures 1–4 retain their plotted content.

improvement.justification: V1 presents Theorem 4.1 as a meaningful large-mini-batch guarantee; v2 demonstrates that its assumptions force full-batch training and supplies a proved failure example. Correcting this central misstatement substantially improves scientific reliability. The Lemma H.1 correction and added MNIST evidence provide further benefits, although the nonlinear experiment remains qualitative support outside the linear theory.
